entities.bio: Founded 2022, Tokyo, by Yuki Nono (CEO) — former researcher at Carnegie Mellon University and Tohoku University. Private; backed by Japanese VCs. Core product: vision-based tactile fingertip sensors that give robots a sense of touch via embedded cameras and AI, rather than traditional strain-gauge sensors.

entities.name: SB Neo
entities.desc: SoftBank's newest AI entity — a neocloud play targeting the US enterprise AI market launched just days before this landscape was updated. SB Neo's thesis: Japanese-owned, US-sited AI cloud infrastructure gives enterprises an alternative to the US Big Three hyperscalers (AWS, Azure, GCP) that is less subject to US government political pressure, while also being more sovereign than Chinese-backed alternatives. SoftBank's Vision Fund portfolio of 400+ companies provides a natural enterprise customer base for SB Neo services. The neocloud category (CoreWeave, Lambda Labs, Oracle Cloud AI) is crowded; SB Neo's differentiation will depend on Arm chip integration (SoftBank's ARM stake) and SoftBank's ability to pre-commit Vision Fund portfolio companies as anchor tenants.
entities.bio: Founded July 2026, as a joint venture between SoftBank Corp (51%) and SoftBank Group (49%). Operates as a US-targeted neocloud company, positioning itself as a Japanese-backed alternative AI cloud platform for enterprise workloads in North America. No public CEO appointment as of August 2026.

entities.name: Micron Hiroshima
entities.desc: The only US DRAM manufacturing presence in Asia — a strategic anchor in the US-Japan semiconductor alliance. Micron's Hiroshima facility is one of two locations (with Taichung, Taiwan) producing HBM2e and HBM3e memory stacks for Nvidia, AMD, and Intel AI accelerators. **HBM supercycle:** Each new generation of AI training chip (Nvidia H100→H200→B200) uses 2–4x more HBM than its predecessor; Micron Hiroshima is capacity-constrained into 2026. **CHIPS Act adjacency:** Micron is simultaneously building a $100B US HBM fab (New York State) with US CHIPS Act subsidy, but Hiroshima remains critical for near-term HBM supply. The Elpida acquisition (2013, from bankruptcy) was Micron's entry into Japan's DRAM industry — an inflection point that made Hiroshima the de facto US memory manufacturing outpost in Japan.
entities.bio: Micron Technology's Japan manufacturing subsidiary, located in Higashihiroshima. Micron Technology (founded 1978, Boise ID, NASDAQ: MU) is the only remaining US-owned DRAM and NAND manufacturer. The Hiroshima facility has produced DRAM since 1980 (acquired from Elpida Memory, 2013) and now produces HBM (High Bandwidth Memory) for AI accelerators.

entities.name: Tower Semiconductor Japan
entities.zh: タワーセミコンダクター日本
entities.desc: Specialty analog and RF semiconductor foundry, relevant in this landscape for its Japan manufacturing footprint in a geopolitically important category. Tower's Agrate (Italy), Newport Beach (US), and Nishiwaki (Japan) fabs produce analog chips for imaging sensors, automotive ADAS radar, and power management — critical inputs for AI vision systems and autonomous vehicle radars. Japan's analog chip supply chain is a quiet strategic asset: Japanese firms (Shin-Etsu, SUMCO for wafers; Tower, Renesas for fab) form a nearly complete analog supply chain that supplements the TSMC-centered digital logic chain.
entities.bio: Tower Semiconductor's Japan subsidiary, operating fabs previously acquired from Panasonic. Tower Semiconductor (founded 1993, Migdal HaEmek, Israel; listed NASDAQ TSEM) is a specialty foundry for analog, RF, and mixed-signal chips. Intel attempted to acquire Tower for $5.4B (2022) but abandoned the deal in 2023.

entities.name: Hitachi
entities.desc: Japan's largest industrial conglomerate, executing a focused AI transformation under CEO Kojima's 'Social Innovation Business' strategy. **Lumada:** Hitachi's AI and digital twin platform for industrial customers — deployed in railways (predictive track maintenance), manufacturing (AI quality inspection), and energy (grid optimization). Lumada revenue exceeded ¥1T ($6.7B) in FY2024, growing faster than the group average. **GlobalLogic integration:** The $9.6B GlobalLogic acquisition (2021) gives Hitachi 25,000+ software engineers — dramatically expanding its software-first AI delivery capability beyond traditional hardware. **Hitachi Energy:** AI-driven grid management tools for energy transition infrastructure — a structural growth market as data centers (and humanoid robot charging networks) increase power grid demand. **Hitachi High-Tech x Powrex physical AI battery coating (Aug 20, 2026):** Hitachi High-Tech completed a demonstration with Powrex applying its HMAX Industry physical AI (PROACCELA process informatics + XRF/SEM analysis) to optimize cathode-coating conditions for all-solid-state batteries — a step toward commercializing a Lab-to-Fab process aimed at cutting the specialized-engineer bottleneck in battery scale-up ahead of the market's expected takeoff around 2030.

entities.name: Toshiba
entities.desc: Japan's most significant corporate governance failure of the 21st century — now a private company working to rebuild post-privatization (Oct 2023). Toshiba sold its NAND flash memory business (now Kioxia) in 2018 following nuclear-subsidiary (Westinghouse) losses; sold Toshiba Medical to Canon (2016); sold its consumer electronics brand to various buyers. **Remaining assets:** Industrial infrastructure (nuclear, water, rail), Toshiba Tec, and a ~40% stake in Kioxia. Post-privatization JIP's mandate is to restructure and eventually relist. Toshiba's trajectory is cautionary context for Japanese corporate AI transformation: a company that led in semiconductors, nuclear, and consumer electronics and failed to manage the transition to software-first competition.
entities.bio: Founded 1939 (merger of Tokyo Shibaura Electric and others), Kawasaki. Privatized October 2023 by Japan Industrial Partners (JIP) consortium after years of financial scandals and governance crises. Former CEO: Taro Shimada (post-privatization). Principal subsidiaries: Toshiba Tec (POS systems), Toshiba Infrastructure Systems, and minority stakes in Kioxia (NAND flash).

entities.name: Disco
entities.desc: A monopoly position in a critical but invisible step: slicing completed semiconductor wafers into individual chips (dicing). Every AI chip in this landscape — Nvidia H100, Huawei Ascend, CXMT DRAM — is cut from a silicon wafer using a Disco dicing saw. **AI demand flywheel:** More chips → more dicing required → more Disco equipment sold. Disco also makes wafer thinning grinders critical for 3D chip stacking (CoWoS, SoIC), which is the packaging technology that enables HBM3 and next-generation 3D AI chips. Disco's ~80% global market share in dicing means it has near-monopoly leverage over the timing of new chip production ramps. The company's unique internal economy ('Will' allocation system — all internal transactions priced at market rates) is a widely cited management case study.
entities.bio: Founded 1937, Ota City, Tokyo. CEO: Kazuma Sekiya. Listed TSE (6146). World's dominant maker of dicing saws, grinders, and laser cutters for semiconductor wafer slicing and thinning. ~80% global market share in dicing saws. Revenue FY2024 ~¥320B ($2.1B).

entities.name: GPIF
entities.zh: 年金積立金管理運用独立行政法人
entities.py: Nenkin Tsumitatekin Kanri Un'yō Dokuritsu Gyōsei Hōjin
entities.desc: The world's largest pension fund — GPIF's portfolio decisions are among the most consequential in global capital markets. As of mid-2026, GPIF holds ~25% in domestic equities (TSE Prime), 25% in international equities, 25% in domestic bonds, and 25% in international bonds. **AI exposure:** GPIF's domestic equity portfolio includes every major Japanese company in this landscape (Hitachi, Fanuc, TEL, Shin-Etsu, Renesas). Its international equity portfolio includes Nvidia, Microsoft, Apple — the primary AI infrastructure companies. **Passive vs. active:** GPIF runs mostly passive indexed strategies, meaning AI sector outperformance directly boosts GPIF returns but GPIF cannot dynamically overweight AI. ESG investing standards have been a controversial constraint on certain defense-adjacent holdings.

entities.name: JPYC
entities.desc: Japan's first legally compliant JPY stablecoin — issued under Japan's Fund Settlement Act, which requires stablecoin issuers to be licensed financial institutions. **AZ-COM Maruwa payroll pilot:** JPYC partnered with AZ-COM Maruwa (a major Amazon Japan logistics company) to pilot paying delivery drivers in JPYC — the first stablecoin payroll implementation in Japan, testing Japanese regulators' appetite for crypto-native payroll infrastructure. **Regulatory readiness:** Japan's Payment Services Act amendment (2023) created one of the world's clearest legal frameworks for stablecoin issuance; JPYC is positioned as the most compliance-ready JPY stablecoin for the opening of institutional digital asset markets in Japan in 2025–2026. Circle (USDC) as investor signals international stablecoin infrastructure convergence. **¥1,000,000 transaction cap lifted (confirmed Aug 24, 2026):** The FSA removed the per-transaction ceiling that had confined second-category Funds Transfer Service Providers like JPYC to retail micropayments since 2023, paired with the FSA's new dedicated Crypto/Stablecoin Division to supervise the larger flows now permitted. JPYC can now structurally compete for B2B settlement and treasury business, though trust-bank-backed JPYSC (SBI Shinsei Trust Bank) retains a stronger legal claim to reserves under trust law.
entities.bio: Founded 2021, Tokyo, by Noritaka Okabe (岡部典孝, CEO). Private; backed by Circle (USDC issuer), SBI Holdings, and others. Japan's first and only legally compliant JPY-pegged stablecoin (under Japan's Fund Settlement Act). JPYC Inc. is the issuer.

entities.name: AZ-COM Maruwa
entities.zh: AZ-COM丸和ホールディングス
entities.desc: Japan's largest independent Amazon delivery partner — roughly 20% of Amazon Japan's last-mile delivery volume passes through Maruwa's network. **JPYC payroll pilot:** Partnered with JPYC to pilot driver compensation in JPY stablecoins — Japan's first stablecoin payroll implementation, addressing the endemic driver wage underpayment problem in Japan's trucking sector. **2024 Logistics Law Reform:** Japan's mandatory 'Truck Driver Working Hours' legislation (April 2024) — the so-called '2024 logistics problem' — capped truck driver overtime and created acute capacity shortages; Maruwa's scale and Amazon relationship give it pricing power to offset higher labor costs but also pressure to adopt automation faster than smaller peers. AZ-COM Maruwa's interest in JPYC is as much about reducing payroll processing friction as it is about crypto adoption.

Japan's largest independent logistics company not affiliated with a major telecom or trading house; principal customer is Amazon Japan, for which Maruwa operates a significant portion of last-mile delivery in Japan.

entities.name: Advantest
entities.desc: World leader in semiconductor automated test equipment (ATE), with dominant share in testers for AI accelerators and HBM — making it one of the highest-beta AI names on the Tokyo exchange. Fell sharply in the July 24, 2026 AI-valuation rout alongside Tokyo Electron and Kioxia. Reports earnings the week of July 28 alongside SCREEN Holdings and Tokyo Electron, into a Nikkei that has lost more than 7% in July and slid into correction — making its order commentary a key read on whether AI-test demand is actually softening or just being repriced. **Q1 FY2026 results, first of the equipment gauntlet (#60, Jul 29 2026):** Reported record Q1 profit — EPS $1.51, net margin 33.2%, ROE 55.98% — on strong demand, favorable product mix and FX gains across CPU, GPU, custom-ASIC and networking testers. Management raised its view of the SoC tester market and said capacity expansion is being pulled forward. Shares still fell 1.22% to ¥25,200, as investors focused on a cautious margin outlook rather than the record top line — the first print in the Advantest (Jul 29) → Tokyo Electron (Jul 30) → Kioxia (Jul 31) equipment/memory earnings sequence that follows the July 28 CXMT-triggered sell-off. **FY2026 guidance raised 35% (#62, Jul 29-31 2026):** Follow-through from the Q1 print: management lifted full-year operating-profit guidance to ¥846.0bn on ¥1.714tn revenue — implying roughly 70% YoY growth, up from a prior forecast of about 26%, and above the ~42% consensus had modeled — after AI-inference tester demand outran what the company assumed as recently as April. Advantest also raised its view of the global semiconductor tester market to $13.0–14.5bn for the year, a record and about 19% above its April forecast. Shares jumped as much as 10.9% intraday on the update, part of a broader Nikkei rally (+4.0% Jul 31) that also lifted Tokyo Electron and Kioxia — a reversal from the cautious Jul 29 reaction and a reminder that the stock is trading on forward order-book signals as much as trailing results. **Nvidia-beat rally fades intraday (#90, Aug 27, 2026):** Rose in early Tokyo trade after Nvidia's blowout Q2 report before reversing to close down 1.96% as the broader Nikkei chip-stock rally faded into profit-taking — another data point that Advantest's high AI-beta cuts both ways within a single session, not just over weeks.

entities.desc: US enterprise AI agent platform expanding to Japan through SoftBank's distribution partnership. Sierra's core product replaces traditional IVR and chatbot systems with AI agents that can handle end-to-end customer service conversations with context and decision-making autonomy. **Japan market strategy:** SoftBank's exclusive distribution partnership gives Sierra immediate access to SoftBank's enterprise client base (Japan's largest telecom with 200M+ service interactions/year) without needing to build a Japan sales team from scratch. **Competitive position:** Competes with Salesforce Agentforce, Oracle, and Japanese domestic vendors (PKSHA, Fujitsu) in the Japanese enterprise AI agent market. Sierra is relevant to this landscape because the SoftBank partnership pattern (US AI startup + SoftBank exclusive Japan distribution) has become a repeating template in Japan's AI market after the OpenAI (SB OAI Japan) precedent.

entities.name: Cabinet Office (CEFP)
entities.zh: 内閣府・経済財政諮問会議
entities.desc: Drafting body for the annual Basic Policy on Economic and Fiscal Management and Reform (骨太の方針). The Takaichi cabinet approved its first edition July 21, 2026: 'responsible and proactive fiscal policy,' ~¥370tn in public-private investment into strategic sectors including AI and semiconductors through FY2040, targets of >1% real and >3% nominal growth, and — notably — removal of the phrase 'fiscal consolidation' in favor of a stable-reduction anchor on the debt-to-GDP ratio. Bond market response was wary, with the long-term rate near 30-year highs and BOJ-independence questions unresolved ahead of the July 30 MPM. **Approval rating slide (#58, Jul 26-27 2026):** A Yomiuri poll fielded Jul 24-26 showed cabinet approval falling to 57% from 69% in June — the first sub-60% reading since Takaichi took office — with disapproval of cost-of-living policy rising to 71% from 56%. The government has delayed its pledged cut to the 8% food consumption-tax rate amid intra-LDP resistance and bond-market sensitivity, leaving the honebuto's ¥370tn growth pledge harder to square with near-term household relief. **FY2026 GDP forecast cut as Korea, Taiwan overtake Japan in exports (#70, Aug 7, 2026):** A Nikkei Asia analysis showed South Korea ($496.3bn) and Taiwan ($416.6bn) each surpassed Japan ($384.4bn) in total H1 2026 exports for the first time, as AI-chip demand drove South Korean semiconductor exports (including SSDs) up 162.6% YoY to $192.4bn — already exceeding all of 2025. Japan's exposure is concentrated in semiconductor materials and manufacturing equipment (Tokyo Electron, Shin-Etsu, SUMCO) rather than the AI logic/memory chips themselves (Samsung, SK Hynix, TSMC) capturing the demand surge. The Cabinet Office response: its FY2026 real GDP growth forecast was cut to 0.9% from an earlier 1.3%, even as South Korea raised its own 2026 growth forecast from 2.0% to 3.0% — a direct trade-competitiveness read-through for the honebuto's ¥370tn strategic-investment pledge, and a reminder that Noetra/Rapidus's payoff is still years from showing up in the export data. **Preliminary Q2 GDP due (Aug 17, 2026):** The Economic and Social Research Institute's first preliminary April-June GDP estimate — the reference data point for both the honebuto's ¥370tn growth pledge and the BOJ's September policy decision — was released today; private-sector consensus (10-institution average) pointed to a third consecutive quarterly expansion near +2.1% annualized, with private consumption as the primary driver and a mild drag from softer exports. **Bond rout puts the honebuto's funding math at risk (#82, Aug 19, 2026):** The 10-year JGB yield pushed toward 2.95–3% this week, a level last seen in 1996 and the exact threshold the government used as its budget assumption, with an early-August 10-year auction drawing the weakest demand in a year. A sustained move above 3% would push debt-servicing costs past the ¥31tn ($195bn) currently budgeted, squeezing room for the honebuto's own ¥370tn pledge. The immediate flashpoint is Takaichi's plan to cut the consumption tax on food to 1% for two years without an identified offsetting revenue source, even as she maintains overall JGB issuance will stay unchanged — a combination bond investors are pricing skeptically given debt already above 200% of GDP, while LDP conservatives simultaneously press her to curb spending. **IP Strategy Headquarters: draft AI training-data disclosure code (#82, Aug 18, 2026):** A separate Cabinet Office body, the Intellectual Property Strategy Headquarters (知的財産戦略本部), unveiled a draft 'comply or explain' principles code for generative-AI (生成AI, seisei AI) developers, built on the AI-related technology law enacted May 2025. Three principles: public disclosure of models used, training data, and collection methods (sensitive data exempted); domain-specific disclosure to rights holders alleging infringement; and a duty to respond to user requests about possible copyright infringement. The code is non-binding — businesses may comply or publicly explain why they do not — a soft-law complement to Japan's copyright statute rather than new hard regulation. **Code formally adopted (#89, Aug 25, 2026):** The government adopted the revised 'Principle-Code for Protection of Intellectual Property and Transparency for the Appropriate Use of Generative AI' — moving from the Aug 18 draft to a Cabinet-level adoption after a Dec 2025–Jan 2026 public consultation. The adopted code applies to generative-AI developers and providers whose systems are offered in Japan or to Japanese nationals, including foreign firms, and sets concrete compliance expectations: respecting paywalls and robots.txt, avoiding pirate sites, retaining training logs, taking technical measures against infringing outputs, and establishing rights-holder contact points. As a comply-or-explain framework it carries no statutory penalty, but it gives Japanese rights holders and regulators a reference standard to cite in disputes with both domestic and foreign AI developers — a distinct escalation from the draft-stage coverage in that it is now the operative document companies will be measured against.

entities.name: Sakana AI
entities.desc: Japan's most internationally prominent AI research lab, founded by two of the most credentialed AI researchers in the world (David Ha + Llion Jones, Transformer co-inventor). **Evolutionary model merging:** Sakana AI's primary research direction is 'AI for AI' — using evolutionary algorithms and model merging to automatically compose or improve existing foundation models without gradient descent retraining, offering potentially 10x+ compute reduction versus training from scratch. **Sovereignty through post-training:** Rather than compete on frontier pretraining compute, Sakana fine-tunes and orchestrates other labs' open-weight models (Moonshot AI's Kimi, Google's Gemma) into Japan-specific products — its free Sakana Translate service, upgraded Aug 21 to the new-generation Namazu model, beat rival translation services in head-to-head evaluation on culturally specific Japanese text. **AI Scientist (2024):** Published a paper on an AI system that autonomously generates, runs, and writes up machine learning research experiments — widely cited as the first plausible automated AI research system. **Funding trajectory:** The $430M raise at $1B+ valuation (2024) makes it the largest single venture round for a Japan-based AI startup in history.
entities.bio: Founded June 2023, Tokyo, by David Ha (CEO) — former Research Director at Google DeepMind — and Llion Jones — co-author of the seminal 2017 'Attention Is All You Need' paper (co-inventor of the Transformer architecture). As Japan's enterprise AI cloud market consolidates, KDDI competes with SoftBank (SB Neo, SB OAI), NTT Group (NTT Data, NTT Research), and US hyperscalers (AWS, Azure, GCP) for enterprise AI infrastructure wallet share.

entities.name: SB Intuitions
entities.desc: SoftBank's standalone Japanese-language LLM effort — the entity that built SoftBank's proprietary Japanese-language AI models before being merged into the Noetra consortium in early 2026. **HyperStar series:** Trained a family of Japanese-language LLMs (HyperStar 1–4) on SoftBank's corpus of Japanese telecom-customer data and public Japanese text. The models were positioned as Japan-specific alternatives to GPT-4 for privacy-sensitive enterprise workloads. **Noetra absorption:** When SoftBank, Sony, NEC, and Honda formally created Noetra in 2026, SB Intuitions' models and team became the core AI research group within the larger consortium — Tamba's departure from CEO of SB Intuitions to become CEO of Noetra was the clearest signal of the organizational restructuring.

entities.name: Institute of Science Tokyo
entities.desc: Japan's foremost STEM university and a primary source of AI and semiconductor research talent. **AI and robotics research:** Faculty research groups at Institute of Science Tokyo (particularly in machine learning, robotics, and quantum computing) are among Japan's most internationally cited. The Nishimori lab (quantum annealing, JIJ Inc. spinout), Matsuo lab (AI ethics and LLM), and Hattori lab (materials informatics) are examples of high-impact research groups. **TSMC collaboration:** Tokyo Tech was a founding partner in the TSMC 'Design Center Alliance' in Japan — linking Japanese universities to TSMC's advanced process nodes for chip design education. As Japan's domestic semiconductor and AI industries scale, Institute of Science Tokyo is the primary upstream supplier of PhD-level talent for Rapidus, Preferred Networks, Sakana AI, and similar companies.
entities.bio: Formally established October 1, 2024, Tokyo, by the merger of Tokyo Institute of Technology (Tokyo Tech, founded 1881) and Tokyo Medical and Dental University (TMDU, founded 1928). Japan's most internationally ranked STEM research university (QS World University Rankings Top 20 for engineering). President: Mitsuhiro Yanagida.

entities.name: Stockmark
entities.desc: Japanese NLP and LLM company with a differentiated data asset: a 220B-token corpus of Japanese web text curated specifically for enterprise language understanding tasks (financial news, corporate filings, regulatory documents). The data moat is the core value proposition — most international LLMs (including GPT-4) have relatively thin Japanese representation in their pretraining data. **Anews:** B2B intelligence product that uses the Stockmark LLM to surface strategic signals from Japanese corporate and regulatory text — used by major Japanese financial institutions and conglomerates. **LLM licensing model:** Stockmark licenses its Japanese LLM to enterprises that need data sovereignty for Japanese financial/legal text, where general-purpose US models face regulatory constraints on where data is processed.
entities.bio: Founded April 2016, Tokyo, by Tatsu Hayashi (CEO) and three engineers. Private; backed by SBI Investment and other Japanese VCs. Core product: Anews (Japanese language business intelligence and NLP platform) and Stockmark LLM — a Japanese-language LLM trained on a 220B-token domestic Japanese web corpus.

entities.zh: パランティア・テクノロジーズ

Palantir is listed in this landscape because its Japan defense and enterprise contracts make it a direct participant in Japan's AI-enabled defense transformation, alongside domestic players like MHI, Kawasaki, and Hitachi.

entities.name: Ministry of Defense (Japan)
entities.desc: Japan's defense ministry, overseeing the Japan Self-Defense Forces (JSDF, 自衛隊). Nikkei reported Aug 5, 2026 that the ministry is weighing adoption of US AI platforms — Palantir's Maven Smart System and Anduril's Lattice AI — for battlefield data fusion, target identification, and drone-swarm coordination, paired with a proposed Sakana AI-built domestic command layer to arbitrate system selection and limit classified-data exposure to foreign contractors. Broader ambition described in the report: integrating AI into missile defense, air-defense coordination, and swarm-drone control. Framed as a speed-of-decision and US-interoperability play amid regional security pressure (North Korea missile activity, China's East China Sea/Indo-Pacific exercises).

entities.name: Toyota Motor Corporation
entities.desc: World's #1 automaker and Japan's largest company, undergoing a multi-year software-defined vehicle and AI transformation. **Woven by Toyota:** Dedicated software and AV subsidiary; Woven Planet (now Woven by Toyota) acquired Lyft's AV division (2021) and is developing the Arene OS (vehicle operating system) and Woven City (living lab for autonomous mobility in Susono, Shizuoka). **Multi-path AV strategy:** Toyota is simultaneously developing ADAS (through Woven by Toyota), investing in Waymo (via Woven Capital), partnering with Pony.ai (autonomous trucking), and licensing Momenta's technology — reflecting a deliberate multi-partner strategy rather than an in-house-only bet. **Preferred Networks partnership:** Toyota is a cornerstone investor in PFN (deep learning for factory robotics and quality inspection); PFN's MN-Core chips are embedded in Toyota production lines. **EV transition:** Toyota's slower-than-rivals EV pivot is partially offset by its hybrid (HEV/PHEV) dominance — in 2025, hybrids represented ~70% of Toyota global sales, insulating it from early EV market softness that hit BYD and NIO.

entities.name: National Cyber Director (Japan)
entities.desc: Japan's top cybersecurity policy office, currently led by Yoichi Iida — a former six-year chair of the OECD Committee on Digital Economy Policy and architect of the 2023 G7 Hiroshima AI Process. **AI export-control exposure disclosed:** In an August 10, 2026 Kyodo News interview, Iida confirmed that the June 12, 2026 US Commerce Department directive suspending global access to Anthropic's Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models disrupted Japan's own government vulnerability-scanning operations — the first time a senior allied-government official has publicly attributed a national-security operational disruption to a unilateral US AI export-control action. **Active Cyber Defense Act:** Japan's law authorizing the National Police Agency and Self-Defense Forces to preemptively neutralize hostile cyber infrastructure takes effect October 1, 2026; Iida called integration of frontier AI into that preemptive posture 'inevitable' given AI-compressed vulnerability-to-exploit timelines, while warning Japan should not depend on any single AI vendor.

entities.bio: Founded 1916, Tokyo. One of the world's largest bearing manufacturers, with a long-standing precision-components business spanning automotive, industrial machinery, and railways. Listed TSE (6471). Has been developing actuators for humanoid robots since at least 2025 as a new growth line beyond its core bearings business.
entities.desc: **MOU with humanoid AI robot startup Atom (Aug 20, 2026):** NSK and Atom signed a comprehensive partnership to build a domestic humanoid robot supply chain, pairing NSK's precision-actuator manufacturing with Atom's AI and robot platform. The two-pronged deal covers (1) installing NSK actuators in Atom's humanoid machines for real-world verification feeding back into NSK's mass-production development, and (2) jointly collecting physical AI data at NSK factories using Atom's humanoids to train physical AI foundation models. The rationale is explicit import-substitution: both companies cite over-reliance on overseas actuator and component supply as a risk to a domestic humanoid industry.

entities.name: Atom
entities.bio: Japanese startup developing humanoid AI robots and the underlying physical AI foundation models. Founding details not yet fully public; positioned as a domestic alternative to overseas humanoid platforms (e.g. Figure, Unitree).
entities.desc: **MOU with NSK for domestic humanoid supply chain (Aug 20, 2026):** Partnered with precision-bearing maker NSK to jointly test NSK actuators in Atom's humanoid robots and to collect physical AI training data at NSK manufacturing sites. The deal is framed as solving humanoid mass-production bottlenecks (actuator supply, real-world training data) by combining a robotics/AI startup with an established domestic component manufacturer rather than relying on overseas suppliers.

entities.name: Powrex
entities.bio: Japanese manufacturer of powder-processing equipment (mixing, granulation, coating) serving pharmaceuticals, food, chemicals, and battery materials industries.
entities.desc: **Physical AI demonstration with Hitachi High-Tech (Aug 20, 2026):** Completed a joint demonstration applying Hitachi High-Tech's HMAX Industry physical AI (PROACCELA process informatics plus XRF/SEM measurement) to Powrex's fluidized-bed coating equipment, identifying optimal coating conditions for all-solid-state battery cathode materials. The companies plan to commercialize the approach as a Lab-to-Fab offering ahead of the all-solid-state battery market's expected scale-up around 2030.
